About NORML

Since its founding in 1970, NORML has been the principal national advocate for legalizing marijuana. During the 1970s, NORML led the successful efforts to decriminalize minor marijuana offenses in 11 states and significantly lower penalties in all others. Though the decriminalization movement eventually fell victim to the "war on drugs," NORML has remained the nation’s principal organization dedicated to ending marijuana prohibition.

Today NORML serves as an informational resource to the national media on marijuana-related stories; lobbies state and federal legislators to permit the medical use of marijuana and to reject recent attempts to treat minor marijuana offenses more harshly; and serves as the umbrella group for a national network of citizen activists committed to ending marijuana prohibition.

A 5-person staff at the NORML national office in Washington, DC, headed by Executive Director (and NORML founder) R. Keith Stroup, serves as the national clearinghouse for marijuana law reform efforts and information nationwide.

NORML Board of Directors (http://www.norml.org/about/bios.shtml)

The 19-member NORML Board of Directors is chaired by Dan Viets of Columbia, Missouri. Mr. Viets is a criminal defense lawyer and long-time marijuana law reform advocate. The board includes prominent scientists and researchers, including Harvard Professor Lester Grinspoon, M.D.; CUNY Professor John Morgan, M.D.; Nobel Laureate Kary Mullis, Ph.D, (Chemistry);

Tufts University Professor Louis Lasagna, M.D. and producer Ann Druyan, and writer Barbara Ehrenreich, as well as other distinguished Americans.

NORML Legal Committee (http://www.norml.org/legal/norml_lc.shtml)

NORML also maintains a Legal Committee comprised of criminal defense attorneys who are committed to ending marijuana prohibition and assisting those who are arrested on marijuana charges. The NORML Amicus Curiae Committee (http://www.norml.org/legal/amcur.html) files "amicus curiae" briefs in marijuana-related cases involving important or novel legal issues.

NORML Internships (http://www.norml.org/about/interns.shtml)

The National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws (NORML) and the NORML Foundation are seeking students for fall, winter, spring and summer internships to work in the national office on progressive marijuana law reform.
